hybrid_architecture_considered_and_rejec.proposal: Use Candidate A's (QUERY_ANALYSIS_PROMPT) entity extraction for entities, Candidate B (STRUCTURED_EXTRACTION_PROMPT) for intent/constraints/normalization/source-prediction.
hybrid_architecture_considered_and_rejec.why_rejected: Both Candidate A and Candidate B are LLM calls against the SAME model (nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b) - Candidate A is NOT a cheap deterministic extractor, it is a second, differently-prompted, unconstrained (no Pydantic entity schema) LLM call. A 2-call hybrid would roughly DOUBLE latency (already the worst-failing gate at P50 14.5s / P95 61.9s for ONE call) for a 5.2-point entity F1 gain that closure-round prompt/taxonomy fixes (B_VS_G_RULE, DI_VS_E_RULE, target-default entity typing) already recovered most of (from an 11.9-14pt gap down to 5.2pts) at ZERO extra latency cost. Given latency is explicitly a product-critical gate for an interactive upstream stage, adding a second call to chase the remaining entity gap is the wrong tradeoff this round. Revisit only if a genuinely cheap/fast supplementary entity mechanism (e.g. the dictionary matcher assessed in item 13, if the benchmark is extended with out-of-table gold examples to fairly test it) can close the gap without a second LLM round-trip.

latency_profiling_finding.method: Direct inspection of extract_candidate_b's raw LLM response content (not just the parsed JSON) via a live single-call test.
latency_profiling_finding.finding: The frozen model (nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b) is a reasoning-tuned model that frequently emits an extensive chain-of-thought preamble (observed: 9234 raw characters of step-by-step reasoning text) BEFORE the JSON answer, sometimes exhausting the full max_tokens=2048 budget on reasoning alone and truncating the JSON entirely (directly explains several of the empty/truncated-response schema failures seen throughout this closure pass, not just an unrelated flakiness). This - not network/queue time - is the dominant latency contributor for a single call.
latency_profiling_finding.mitigation_attempted: A '/no_think' prompt prefix (a documented pattern for some reasoning-tuned model families) was tried live: it suppressed the reasoning trace and cut single-call latency from ~96s to ~21s in one test, but a second identical test with the same prefix still produced the full chain-of-thought - i.e. the suppression is UNRELIABLE on this endpoint/model as configured, not a safe production change to make on the strength of 2 data points.
latency_profiling_finding.decision: NOT adopted this closure pass - reported honestly as a well-diagnosed but not-yet-safely-fixable latency root cause, rather than shipping an unreliable prompt trick. A future round should verify whether the NVIDIA NIM endpoint exposes a structured, reliable reasoning-disable parameter (e.g. an extra_body chat_template_kwargs flag) rather than a prompt-text convention.

overall_item_18_verdict: 9 of 10 gates PASS on the final frozen config (entity F1, normalization, intent systematic confusion, constraints, phase/status canonicalization, gene/protein/target representation, empty-response handling, structured-output reliability, token accounting, ambiguity fail-safe - that's actually all but one). The ENTITY F1 gate flipped from FAIL to PASS this round: after the exhaustive-entity-scan prompt fix (targeting the precisely-diagnosed 'using X inhibitors trailing clause' drop), Candidate B's entity F1 (0.901) now EXCEEDS Candidate A's baseline (0.889) - the regression that originally reopened Phase 2 is resolved. 1 gate still FAILS: latency - root-caused this round (dominant cost is chain-of-thought reasoning generation from the underlying reasoning-tuned model, confirmed by direct raw-output inspection) but not safely fixable within this round's time budget; a suppression trick was tested and found unreliable, so it was correctly NOT shipped rather than forced. Candidate B (post-closure-fixed, prompt v4) is FROZEN as the working single-call architecture. A 2-call hybrid with Candidate A's entity extraction remains REJECTED and is now doubly unnecessary since the entity gap that motivated considering it is closed. Phase 2 remains OPEN on the latency gate alone (plus general small-n statistical caution, dev n=45) - every other item-18 gate now passes on the final frozen config. See docs/v2/PHASE2_CLOSURE_REPORT.md for the full accounting.
